explain.say: In April 1955, in the Indonesian hill city of Bandung, President Sukarno welcomed leaders of twenty-nine Asian and African states, speaking for more than half of humanity. Most had been colonies only a few years before. Look at the timeline. Could newly free nations refuse to pick a side in the Cold War?

explain.say: Now the map. From Bandung grew the Non-Aligned Movement, founded at Belgrade in 1961. Its leading figures were Jawaharlal Nehru of India, Sukarno, Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt and Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana. What do you notice about where these capitals are?

Look at the network. Non-aligned states took help from both sides. The USSR funded Egypt's Aswan Dam, the USA sent food aid to India and aid to Yugoslavia after Tito broke with Stalin. Non-alignment meant not joining military blocs, not staying silent. Why might playing two rivals help a poor country?

See the membership grow: 25 states at Belgrade in 1961, 47 at Cairo in 1964, 75 by 1973, about 120 today. The French writer Alfred Sauvy had coined the phrase Third World in 1952, echoing the Third Estate of 1789: the overlooked majority. In 1964 the Group of 77 began pressing for fairer trade. What did the Third Estate demand in 1789?

items.label: Today
items.ask: How many members does the Non-Aligned Movement have?

explain.say: Now weigh it. Strengths: a strong voice at the UN and anti-colonial solidarity. Limits: India and China, Bandung partners, went to war in 1962, and some members leaned to one bloc. Vijay Prashad calls it a real but limited project. Wonderful thinking. Challenge: name a country today that tries to stay non-aligned.

faq.a: A group of states, founded at Belgrade in 1961, that refused to join either the US-led or Soviet-led military blocs during the Cold War, and pressed for decolonisation, disarmament and fairer economic relations.

faq.q: What happened at the Bandung Conference?
faq.a: In April 1955, 29 Asian and African states met in Bandung, Indonesia, to promote cooperation, oppose colonialism and assert independence from the superpowers. It is seen as the birth of the Third World as a political force.

Partly. It gave newer states a collective voice at the UN and let them gain aid from both blocs, but members sometimes fought each other, as India and China did in 1962, some leaned towards one superpower, and they had little military or economic power.
asks: What were the limits of non-alignment?

faq.q: How many members does the Non-Aligned Movement have?
faq.a: It began with 25 members at Belgrade in 1961, grew to 47 by 1964 and 75 by 1973, and has about 120 member states today.
asks: Does the Non-Aligned Movement still exist?

faq.q: Why did India and China go to war in 1962?
faq.a: A border dispute in the Himalayas, in Aksai Chin and along the McMahon Line, and tensions after the Dalai Lama fled to India in 1959, led to a short war in October and November 1962 that China won. It damaged the idea of Asian solidarity from Bandung.

facts: The Bandung Conference was held in April 1955 with 29 countries.
The Non-Aligned Movement was founded at Belgrade in September 1961.
Alfred Sauvy coined the term Third World in 1952.

quiz.say: The movement grew from 25 members in 1961 to about 120 today. About how many times bigger is that?
quiz.why: 120 divided by 25 is 4.8, about five times.
